name: Recruit and onboard staff
summary: The model manager grew from about 207 staff at the end of 2020 to 328 at the end of 2022, so two talent acquisition partners and their manager ran a steady flow of hires. A hiring manager raises a requisition against the board-approved staffing budget, HR sets the pay band, posts the role or engages a search firm, screens and phone-screens candidates and coordinates two interview rounds with a panel and case study. Offers are approved within the band, background checks and notice periods follow, and HR operations sets up payroll, access and code of conduct onboarding. Calendar slots for panels, candidate notice periods and restarts when no finalist fits make the elapsed time long.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager in one Toronto office, growing quickly from about 100 staff in 2018 toward 300.
baseline.notes: HR information system with an applicant tracking module, outsourced payroll, video interviews from 2020, electronic signature for offers.

trigger: A hiring manager raises a requisition for a budgeted new role or a replacement, under the approved annual budget and headcount plan.
end_state: The new hire has started, is on payroll, has system access requested and is enrolled in code of conduct attestation and mandatory training; or the requisition is cancelled or the offer withdrawn.

volume.seasonality: Peaks after budget approval early in the year and for summer student and graduate starts.

evidence.note: Headcount rose from 207 (end 2020) to 257 (end 2021) and 328 (end 2022), net growth of 50 and 71 a year before turnover; the process map range of 3 to 8 hires a month is kept.

evidence.note: Organisation file role not listed on this process; sets the job level and pay band and builds offers within the board-overseen compensation framework.

roles.department: Financial planning, cost allocation and client billing

roles.title: Hiring manager (manager or director in any department)

evidence.note: The organisation file has no generic hiring manager role. Cost blends its manager (60 to 170 an hour) and managing director (300 to 600) rates, weighted to managers. About 18 hours per hire including interview panel colleagues' time at 5 hires a month.

systems.name: HR information system with outsourced payroll
Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Corporate ERP (general ledger, accounts payable, budgeting)
IT service management and change ticketing tool
Code of conduct, personal trading pre-clearance and attestation system

steps.name: Raise the requisition
steps.description: The hiring manager fills in the requisition in the HR system: title, team, reason (new role or replacement), level, target start date and cost centre, attaches or updates the job description and submits it to talent acquisition.

error.defect_description: Job description out of date or wrong level requested.

evidence.note: Requisition content and the hiring manager's role; times tier C.

steps.name: Check the requisition against the headcount plan
steps.description: The talent acquisition partner checks that the role is in the approved budget and headcount plan for the team or replaces a leaver, that the job description is current and the requisition is complete, and routes it for approval.

control.basis: Board-approved annual budget and staffing plan; the board may not delegate budget approval

evidence.note: HR checks completeness and budget; the model manager Board approves the staffing budget. The 15% unbudgeted share is tier C.

steps.name: Finance approves a position outside the plan
steps.description: The director of financial planning reviews the cost of an unbudgeted role, its effect on the cost recovery budget charged to clients and offsets elsewhere, and approves it, defers it to next year's budget or rejects it.

control.basis: Delegation of financial authority for unbudgeted headcount

evidence.note: Finance approves when extra budget is needed and stricter review applies; rates and times tier C.

steps.name: Head of HR approves the requisition
steps.description: The senior vice president of human resources approves the requisition in the HR system after checking the role against the organisation design and the year's hiring priorities.

control.basis: HR policy: requisition approval before recruiting starts

evidence.note: Senior HR or executive approval of requisitions; times tier C.

steps.name: Set the job level and pay band
steps.description: The total rewards manager evaluates the job against the model manager's job architecture and market survey data, confirms the level and the base salary band and incentive target, and records them on the requisition.

evidence.note: Compensation framework overseen by the Human Resources and Compensation Committee; times tier C.

steps.name: Hold the intake meeting
steps.description: The talent acquisition partner meets the hiring manager to agree the candidate profile, must-have skills, interview panel and assessment, the sourcing plan and whether a search firm is needed for a senior or scarce role.

evidence.note: HR schedules a job intake after approval; the 30% search firm share is tier C, reflecting senior investment hires.

steps.name: Post the role and source candidates
steps.description: The partner writes and posts the advertisement on the careers page, LinkedIn and job boards with the accessibility and accommodation statement, and searches LinkedIn and past applicants for people to approach.

control.basis: Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, Integrated Accessibility Standards (O. Reg. 191/11): notify applicants that accommodation is available

evidence.note: Common practice; the accommodation statement follows Ontario's accessibility employment standard (O. Reg. 191/11), not opened here.

steps.name: Engage a search firm
steps.description: The talent acquisition manager selects a search firm from the approved list, agrees the fee (usually a share of first-year pay) and the brief, and briefs the firm with the hiring manager.

control.basis: Procurement policy: approved supplier list and signed fee agreement

evidence.note: Search firms are used for senior roles in the organisation file's process description; fee basis is common practice.

steps.name: Applications arrive or the search firm builds a slate
steps.description: Applications come in through the HR system over two to three weeks, or the search firm approaches and screens candidates and presents a slate, often after a month.

evidence.note: About 74 candidates enter the process per hire; the one to three week wait is tier C.

steps.name: Screen the applications
steps.description: The partner reads the résumés against the must-have criteria, rejects those that do not fit with a standard message and builds a long list of a dozen or so candidates for phone screens.

error.defect_description: A strong candidate is screened out on keywords.

evidence.note: Only about 11% of candidates pass the first stage; times tier C.

steps.name: Hold phone screens
steps.description: The partner books and holds 20 to 30 minute calls with six to ten candidates to check interest, pay expectations, notice period and fit, and writes short notes for the hiring manager.

evidence.note: Common practice; numbers and times tier C.

steps.name: Hiring manager reviews the shortlist
steps.description: The hiring manager reviews the shortlist and screen notes and chooses three to five candidates to interview, or asks for a different profile.

evidence.note: Common practice; rates and times tier C.

steps.name: Schedule the interviews
steps.description: The partner coordinates calendars of the candidates, hiring manager and panel members, books video or in-office interviews and sends interview guides and candidate packs.

evidence.note: Common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Hold first-round interviews
steps.description: The hiring manager and one colleague interview three to five candidates for about an hour each using the structured guide, score them and agree who goes to the final round.

evidence.note: Interview processes averaged 22 days in Canada, longer at large and government employers; times tier C. Touch minutes include the colleague's time.

steps.name: Hold final panel interviews and assessments
steps.description: Two or three finalists meet a panel of three or four, often including a senior leader, and complete a case study, model test or presentation; panel members score them against the profile.

evidence.note: Group panel interviews add about 5.6 to 6.8 days to hiring; touch minutes include panel members' time and are tier C.

steps.name: Debrief and select the candidate
steps.description: The hiring manager and partner hold the debrief with the panel, compare scores and evidence and select the preferred candidate and a runner-up, or decide that no one fits and sourcing must restart.

evidence.note: About 45% of onsite candidates reach offer stage; the 15% restart rate is tier C.

steps.name: Check references
steps.description: With the candidate's consent the partner calls two or three referees, usually former managers, using a standard question set and records the answers for the hiring manager.

evidence.note: Common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Build the offer within the pay band
steps.description: The total rewards manager proposes base salary, incentive target and any signing or relocation terms within the band, checks internal equity with peers in the same level and prepares the offer approval form.

error.defect_description: Offer breaks internal equity or the band.

evidence.note: Board-overseen compensation framework; times tier C.

steps.name: Head of HR approves the offer
steps.description: The senior vice president of human resources approves the offer terms, or sends them back if they exceed the band or create an equity problem; senior and executive offers go on to the chief executive.

control.basis: Compensation policy: offer approval within band and above-band approval

evidence.note: Offer approval authority is common practice; the model manager's thresholds are not public.

steps.name: Chief executive approves a senior offer
steps.description: For managing director, vice president and executive roles the chief executive reviews and approves the offer, sometimes after a final meeting with the candidate.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: CEO approval of senior appointments

evidence.note: Common practice for senior hires; the model manager's rule is not public.

steps.name: Make the verbal offer and negotiate
steps.description: The partner calls the candidate with the offer, answers questions on pay, pension, benefits and hybrid work, and handles counter-proposals or a counter-offer from the current employer.

evidence.note: Offer acceptance averaged 81% (86% for non-technical roles) (gem_2022); the model manager offers a defined benefit pension and hybrid work (top100). Split of declines and counter-proposals tier C.

steps.name: Issue the written offer and background check consent
steps.description: The partner generates the offer letter and employment agreement from templates, sends them for electronic signature with the background check consent and authorisation forms, and tracks the signed return.

error.defect_description: Wrong salary, title or start date in the letter.

control.basis: Consumer Reporting Act (Ontario): notice and consent before obtaining a consumer report for employment

evidence.note: Written consent before a credit check follows Ontario's Consumer Reporting Act, not opened here; times tier C.

steps.name: Background check provider completes the checks
steps.description: The screening provider runs the criminal record, education, employment history and, for finance roles, credit checks, and reports results through its portal; foreign degrees and employers take longer.

control.basis: Pre-employment screening policy for a financial services employer

evidence.note: Traditional background checks average 7 to 10 days, education verification 7 to 14.

steps.name: Review an adverse background finding
steps.description: The talent acquisition manager reviews the adverse or unverifiable item with the candidate, decides with the hiring manager and legal whether it is relevant to the role and either confirms or withdraws the offer.

evidence.note: Common practice; rates and times tier C.

steps.name: Candidate works out the notice period
steps.description: The new hire resigns and works the notice period with the current employer, usually two to four weeks and up to three months for senior investment staff, while HR prepares for the start date.

evidence.note: Two weeks is the common Canadian minimum; longer notice for senior roles is tier C.

steps.name: Set up the employee record and payroll
steps.description: The HR operations specialist creates the employee record in the HR system, enters pay, incentive target and benefits class, collects tax forms and banking details and sends the new hire to the outsourced payroll provider for the next pay run.

error.defect_description: Wrong salary, benefits class or bank details keyed.

control.basis: Income Tax Act payroll withholding: employee tax credit forms collected at hire

evidence.note: Payroll set-up with federal and provincial tax forms is standard practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Request system access and compliance onboarding
steps.description: The specialist raises the IT access and equipment request based on the role's access profile, orders the building pass and enrols the new hire for code of conduct attestation and personal trading account disclosure.

control.basis: OSC exemption order for the model manager: code of conduct and personal trading restrictions for personnel

evidence.note: Personal trading restrictions and insider trading prohibitions must apply to the model manager personnel; access and attestation steps are handled in their own processes. Times tier C.

steps.name: Run the first-day orientation and mandatory training
steps.description: On the start date the specialist welcomes the new hire, collects signed policy acknowledgements, confirms access works and enrols them in mandatory training: health and safety awareness, workplace harassment, accessibility, code of conduct and the DEI module.

control.basis: Occupational Health and Safety Act (Ontario) and O. Reg. 297/13 awareness training; workplace harassment policy and training

next.condition: new hire started and set up

evidence.note: DEI topics embedded in the model manager's orientation (mgr_ar21); orientation covers policies, paperwork and mandatory training (shrm_onb). The mandatory training list follows Ontario workplace rules, tier C.

exceptions.name: No suitable finalist
exceptions.description: The panel finds no one who fits and sourcing restarts, adding three to six weeks.

exceptions.name: Offer declined or countered
exceptions.description: The candidate declines (turn to the runner-up) or asks for better terms that need new approval.

exceptions.name: Unbudgeted position
exceptions.description: The role is outside the approved headcount plan and finance must approve it; some are deferred.

exceptions.name: Search firm hire
exceptions.description: Senior or scarce roles go to a search firm, which takes longer to present a slate.

exceptions.name: Adverse background finding
exceptions.description: An adverse or unverifiable item is reviewed and about half lead to withdrawal of the offer.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from requisition to the new hire's first day
benchmarks.population: Professional hires at a Canadian public sector investment organisation (author's estimate)

evidence.note: Time to hire (application to acceptance) of 23 to 47 days (gem_2022, bersin_tth) plus requisition approval, sourcing, background checks and a two to twelve week notice period; large and government employers take longer (glassdoor_tth).

benchmarks.population: Employers in the Josh Bersin Company and AMS study

pain_points.description: Booking interview panels with senior investment staff takes weeks, and two interview rounds plus a case study stretch the process.

evidence.note: Panel interviews add about six days.

pain_points.description: Two partners carry a high requisition load during rapid growth, so screening and phone screens queue.

evidence.note: Headcount grew 28% in 2022; queueing is the author's reading.

pain_points.description: Finalists decline or are countered by their employer, sending the search back to the runner-up or to sourcing.
Notice periods for senior investment hires delay start dates by months after the offer.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for senior investment roles.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: 207 full-time employees at 31 December 2020; hired a chief operations officer and filled senior investment and support roles to support more direct and co-investing.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Diversity, equity and inclusion embedded in talent strategy and recruitment; DEI topics embedded in employee orientation and onboarding for new hires; the Human Resources and Compensation Committee oversees the compensation framework.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: In 2022 the model manager team grew from 257 to 328 people, an increase of 28%, to enhance operations, internalise strategies and build systems; operating expenses rose mainly because of headcount.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemptions for the model manager and its investment pools)
sources.supports: The model manager Board may not delegate approval of the model manager's budget, including its budget for staffing; board-approved policies must restrict personal trading and prohibit insider trading by the model manager personnel.

sources.title: The model manager's public purpose inspires its employees (employer review)
sources.supports: 406 full-time employees in 2026; orientation programme for new graduates; performance reviews every six months; defined benefit pension; hybrid work; paid internships; recruits analysts, senior analysts and associates.

sources.title: Why is hiring taking longer? New insights from Glassdoor data
sources.supports: Average interview process of 22.1 days in Canada in 2014, the shortest of the countries studied; hiring times grew 3.3 to 3.7 days since 2009; larger companies and government employers take longer; group panel interviews add about 5.6 to 6.8 days; based on more than 340,000 interview reviews.

sources.title: Time-to-hire rates increasing significantly for almost all roles
sources.supports: Josh Bersin Company and AMS report: average time to hire 44 days in 2023, up from 43 days a year earlier; professional services above average at 47 days; specialised roles and small talent pools take longest.

sources.title: 2022 recruiting benchmarks
sources.supports: Median time to hire 23 days (September 2021 to March 2022, up from 18); 74 candidates per hire; offer acceptance 81% on average (86% for non-technical roles); stage pass-through rates pre-onsite 11%, onsite 34%, offer 45%, hire 81%.

sources.title: The real costs of recruitment
sources.supports: SHRM benchmarking data: average cost per hire nearly US$4,700.

sources.title: What is a job requisition? A full guide and free form template
sources.supports: Hiring manager raises the requisition with title, reason, salary range, start date and budget; HR checks it, the department head approves need and budget, finance approves if extra budget is needed, executives approve senior roles, then HR holds a job intake; approvals can take about a week and stall when no budget exists.

sources.title: Onboarding: process
sources.supports: Preboarding after offer acceptance; orientation covering policies, required paperwork and mandatory training spread over a few days; buddies; onboarding spanning about a year.

sources.title: How long do background checks take
sources.supports: Traditional timelines: criminal database 2 to 3 days, county search 3 to 7, employment verification 5 to 10, education verification 7 to 14; industry average 7 to 10 days for traditional checks.

assumptions: hiring_manager is not in the organisation file; it stands for whichever manager or director owns the role, and its touch minutes include interview panel colleagues' time. Its cost blends manager and managing director rates.
hr_rewards_manager, director_fpa and ceo are organisation file roles that the process map does not list for this process; they set pay bands, approve unbudgeted roles and approve senior offers.

Triggers: the approved budget and headcount plan opens about 60% of requisitions (new roles in a growth period) and applications from candidates and search firms account for the rest; both describe the same hire.

Setting up payroll, access and compliance enrolment runs during the notice period and is marked concurrent; IT account creation, benefits enrolment and the attestation itself are counted in it-service-access, payroll-benefits and code-of-conduct-attestations.

Ontario rules named as controls (accessibility notice to applicants, consent before a credit check, health and safety awareness training) could not be opened because the Ontario e-Laws site refused automated access; they are named from general knowledge and the steps are tier C or B on other sources.

The organisation file's 5 hires a month is below what the model manager's reported growth implies (about 6 in 2021 and 8 in 2022 counting turnover); the process map range is kept and the gap is noted.

Loaded costs come from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, variable pay and a 1.35 loading). Hands-on time of about 45 hours per hire across roles is the author's estimate. The simulated 90th percentile (about 112 days) is below the 150-day estimate because long senior searches and three-month notice periods are a small share of hires.
Web searching ran out while this workflow was researched, so sources were limited to pages fetched by address; most US benchmarks are used only as ranges for a Canadian employer.
